outcomes.name: June Fed rate change
outcomes.description: The market resolves to Change if the upper bound of the target federal funds rate range in the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) statement for the meeting currently scheduled for June 16-17, 2026 differs from the upper bound of the target range set by the most recent prior FOMC statement. Otherwise, the market resolves to No Change. The market also resolves to No Change if the June 16-17, 2026 meeting is canceled, or if no FOMC statement containing a rate decision for that meeting is released by 23:59 ET on July 29, 2026. The target range stated in the FOMC statement for the June 16-17, 2026 meeting determines the result. If that statement is unavailable or does not clearly state the target range, the post-meeting target range upper bound shown on the Federal Reserve's open market operations page determines the result. Resolution uses the initially released decision; later revisions after resolution are not considered. Scheduled meeting dates and source references are provided for convenience and are not binding terms of resolution.

questions.name: May CPI year-over-year
questions.description: The question resolves by assigning Yes to exactly one of Below 4.3%, Exactly 4.3%, or Above 4.3% based on the Bureau of Labor Statistics Consumer Price Index news release for May 2026, currently scheduled for June 10, 2026 at 8:30 AM ET. The relevant value is the non-seasonally adjusted all items Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) percent change over the 12 months ending May 2026, as reported to one decimal place in the official monthly CPI news release. If BLS has not published the May 2026 all items CPI-U figure by July 15, 2026, or if BLS announces that it will not publish the May 2026 all items CPI-U figure, the question instead resolves to the most recently published month's non-seasonally adjusted all items CPI-U 12-month percent change available at that time. If the May 2026 release occurs on a date other than the scheduled date, the rescheduled release is still used for resolution, provided the figure is published by July 15, 2026. Resolution uses the initial published value, not subsequent revisions.

outcomeTemplates.name: {shortNameA} v {shortNameB} on {dateTime}
outcomeTemplates.description: This market compares {modelA} ({shortNameA}) and {modelB} ({shortNameB}) on {dateTime} using Arena's Text Overall leaderboard at https://arena.ai/leaderboard/text/overall-no-style-control, with style control and factuality adjustments off and all models included. Each model is the exact version and configuration identified by its leaderboard name. Renames count only if Arena identifies the same model; replacements and other configurations do not. A relocated or renamed leaderboard counts only if Arena identifies the same Text Overall evaluation. The Snapshot is the latest official leaderboard version public at or before {dateTime}. Proof requires official publication metadata identifying that version or a verifiable timestamped capture of its contents by then. A date alone suffices only if the entire date precedes the deadline in an established timezone. Later captures qualify only if official metadata or earlier captures prove identical contents public by the deadline. Official version order prevails; capture order alone does not order versions. Unresolved conflicts over version selection or required facts leave them unestablished. Comparison favors lower optimistic rank, then higher displayed Arena Score, then more votes. Later criteria apply only if earlier ones are equal. Optimistic rank uses Arena's lower Rank Spread endpoint, or Rank (UB) if absent. If either model has neither, both ranks are one plus the number of other included models whose lower 95% score bound exceeds that model's upper bound, using displayed intervals and precision across all included models. Published ranks otherwise prevail; row rank is no substitute. Scores use displayed point estimates. Optimistic rank can favor a lower score with greater uncertainty. The market resolves to 0.5 if either model is absent, both names identify the same model, the Snapshot or a required fact is unestablished by the evidence cutoff, or the leaderboard was discontinued without a qualifying successor by {dateTime}. Otherwise, it resolves to {shortNameA} if comparison favors {modelA}, to {shortNameB} if it favors {modelB}, and to 0.5 if tied after votes. A resolution to 0.5 pays $0.50 per token on either side. Unused tiebreak values are unnecessary. Evidence is limited to Arena's official records and verifiable timestamped leaderboard captures public by 24 hours after {dateTime}; resolution occurs only after that cutoff. Evidence may authenticate the Snapshot as published, including model identities; corrections, reassignments, and versions first public after {dateTime} are excluded even if their data covers an earlier period. All comparisons use the same Snapshot. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with Arena or any model developer referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:technology|subCategory:N/A|semanticRestriction:This market must compare two specific AI language models on a public performance leaderboard.

outcomeTemplates.name: {period} {award} winner
outcomeTemplates.description: This {field} market covers the {period} {award} (the "Award"). Among editions of one award that {awardingBody} confers or administers with a winner due by {resolutionDeadline}, {period} identifies one by {awardingBody}'s labeling or, failing that, by the year its winner is due; otherwise the Award Result is unestablished. It has one named outcome per listed candidate plus one called Other, which may be registered at any time. Exactly one outcome resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. An entry is one nominee, finalist, or winner of the Award as official channels record it, including a group recorded as one, with every work and person named on it as its nominee or recipient, even jointly, not as a member or representative of a group. A candidate identifies an entry if its Subject unambiguously identifies a work, group, or named person on that entry and no other entry of the Award. Official channels are the publications, events, and broadcasts of {awardingBody} and the Award's conferring body and administrator. The trigger is the earliest verifiable announcement on an official channel of the result: a winner, winners, or that the Award is withheld or not conferred; an announcement is not a trigger if, within one hour after it and before {resolutionDeadline}, it is withdrawn or removed or an official channel contradicts it. Fixing is the earlier of one hour after the trigger and {resolutionDeadline}, or {resolutionDeadline} without a trigger. The Award Result is the winner official channels have named as of fixing; a verifiably later statement supersedes earlier ones on the same channel or made at an event or broadcast, an explicit correction by fixing prevails across channels, other conflicts leave it unestablished, and omission is not a conflict. A candidate registered after the earliest official-channel announcement of a winner of the Award, whether or not it is a trigger, or that identifies no entry at fixing, resolves to No. A candidate finally resolves to No once official channels publish final nominees or finalists none of which it identifies or show it identifies the same entry as an earlier registered candidate. Of the remaining candidates, the earliest registered identifying the one winning entry the Award Result names resolves to Yes; all others resolve to No. Other resolves to Yes if no candidate resolves to Yes, including if the Award Result is unestablished at fixing, names no winner, or names more than one winning entry, such as a tie. Only evidence public by 24 hours after fixing establishes the trigger and the Award Result at fixing; timestamps must prove when contents were public; a Yes resolution occurs only after that cutoff. This market is not sponsored by, endorsed by, or affiliated with any entity referenced. Names and trademarks are descriptive only. metadata=category:culture|subCategory:{field}|semanticRestriction:This market must refer to the single winner of an award or honor, not a selection for office or candidacy.
